m10c-1-1.title: Referents, Estimation and Units, Part 1: Units and Referents

cues.prompt: A phone is about $4\text{ in}$ wide. About how many centimetres is that? Use $1\text{ in} \approx 2.5\text{ cm}$.
cues.working: $4 \times 2.5 = 10\text{ cm}$. An inch is longer than a centimetre, so there are more centimetres than inches.

m10c-1-1-b.title: Referents, Estimation and Units, Part 2: Estimating and Choosing Units

cues.prompt: Which is longer, $5\text{ km}$ or $3\text{ mi}$? Use $1\text{ mi} \approx 1.6\text{ km}$.
cues.working: $3\text{ mi} \approx 3 \times 1.6 = 4.8\text{ km}$, so $5\text{ km}$ is slightly longer.

m10c-1-2.title: Measuring with Rulers and Calipers, Part 1: Reading Rulers

cues.prompt: A bar ends 6 sixteenths past the 1 inch mark. How long is it, in lowest terms?
cues.working: $\dfrac{6}{16} = \dfrac{3}{8}$ (divide both by 2), so the bar is $1\dfrac{3}{8}$ in long.

m10c-1-2-b.title: Measuring with Rulers and Calipers, Part 2: The Vernier Caliper and Curved Lengths

cues.prompt: What does this vernier caliper read?
cues.working: The vernier 0 is just past $15\text{ mm}$, and its 4 lines up: $15 + 0.4 = 15.4\text{ mm}$.

cues.prompt: A string wrapped **3 times** around a jar is $66\text{ cm}$ long. What is the jar’s diameter?

m10c-1-3.title: Converting Within a Measurement System, Part 1: Conversion Factors

cues.prompt: A shelf is $50\text{ in}$ long. How long is it in feet and inches?
cues.working: $50 \div 12 = 4$ remainder $2$, so the shelf is $4\text{ ft}\ 2\text{ in}$.

m10c-1-3-b.title: Converting Within a Measurement System, Part 2: Area and Volume Units

cues.prompt: How many square inches are in $3\text{ ft}^2$?

m10c-1-4.title: Converting Between SI and Imperial Units, Part 1: Conversion Factors

cues.prompt: A board is $8\text{ ft}$ long. How long is it in metres? Use $1\text{ ft} = 0.3048\text{ m}$.
cues.working: $8\,\text{ft} \times \dfrac{0.3048\text{ m}}{1\text{ ft}} \approx 2.44\text{ m}$. A metre is longer than a foot, so the number gets smaller.

m10c-1-4-b.title: Converting Between SI and Imperial Units, Part 2: Rates and Reasonable Answers

cues.prompt: Which is the best estimate of $50\text{ mi}$ in kilometres?
cues.working: $50 \times 1.6 = 80$. A mile is longer than a kilometre, so there are more kilometres than miles.

m10c-1-5.title: Surface Area of Prisms and Cylinders, Part 1: Prisms

cues.prompt: A box is $10\text{ cm}$ long, $4\text{ cm}$ wide and $3\text{ cm}$ high. What is its surface area?

m10c-1-5-b.title: Surface Area of Prisms and Cylinders, Part 2: Cylinders

cues.prompt: A can with radius $3\text{ cm}$ and height $10\text{ cm}$ has **no lid**. How much metal is it made of, to the nearest tenth?
cues.working: One circle and the curved surface: $\pi(3)^2 + 2\pi(3)(10) = 9\pi + 60\pi = 69\pi \approx 216.8\text{ cm}^2$.

m10c-1-6.title: Surface Area of Pyramids, Cones and Spheres, Part 1: Slant Height and Pyramids

cues.prompt: A square pyramid has a base of $6\text{ cm}$ and a height of $4\text{ cm}$. What is its slant height?
cues.working: Half the base is $3$, so $s = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ cm}$.

m10c-1-6-b.title: Surface Area of Pyramids, Cones and Spheres, Part 2: Cones and Spheres

cues.prompt: A ball has a radius of $5\text{ cm}$. What is its surface area, to the nearest tenth?

m10c-1-7.title: Volume of Prisms, Cylinders, Pyramids and Cones, Part 1: Prisms and Cylinders

cues.prompt: A cylinder has radius $3\text{ cm}$ and height $10\text{ cm}$. What is its volume, to the nearest tenth?

m10c-1-7-b.title: Volume of Prisms, Cylinders, Pyramids and Cones, Part 2: Pyramids and Cones

chapters.title: A cone given its slant height

cues.prompt: A cone has radius $3\text{ cm}$ and height $4\text{ cm}$. What is its volume, to the nearest tenth?

m10c-1-8.title: Spheres, Composite Objects and Unknown Dimensions, Part 1: Spheres and Unknown Dimensions

cues.prompt: A sphere has a volume of $36\pi\text{ cm}^3$. What is its radius?

m10c-1-8-b.title: Spheres, Composite Objects and Unknown Dimensions, Part 2: Composite Objects

cues.prompt: A cylinder with radius $2\text{ m}$ and height $6\text{ m}$ has a cone with the same radius and height $3\text{ m}$ on top. What is the total volume, to the nearest tenth?

m10c-2-1.title: The Tangent Ratio, Part 1: Naming the Sides

cues.prompt: In $\triangle PQR$, $\angle R = 90^\circ$, $PR = 12$ and $QR = 5$. What is $\tan P$?
cues.working: From $\angle P$, the **opposite** side is $QR = 5$ and the **adjacent** side is $PR = 12$, so $\tan P = \dfrac{5}{12} \approx 0.42$.

m10c-2-1-b.title: The Tangent Ratio, Part 2: Finding Sides and Angles

cues.prompt: In a right triangle, ${\theta} = 40^\circ$ and the **adjacent** side is $10$ cm. Which expression gives the **opposite** side $x$?

m10c-2-2.title: The Sine and Cosine Ratios, Part 1: SOH CAH TOA

cues.prompt: You know the **hypotenuse** and want the side **adjacent** to ${\theta}$. Which ratio do you use?

m10c-2-2-b.title: The Sine and Cosine Ratios, Part 2: Finding Sides and Angles

cues.prompt: A ramp is $4$ m long and makes an angle of ${12^\circ}$ with the ground. How high does it rise?
cues.working: The ramp is the **hypotenuse** and the rise is **opposite** the angle, so use sine: $h = 4\sin 12^\circ \approx 0.83$ m.

m10c-2-3.title: Solving Right Triangles, Part 1: One Side and One Angle

cues.prompt: In $\triangle PQR$, $\angle R = 90^\circ$, $\angle P = {50^\circ}$ and $PQ = 10$. How long is $QR$, the side **opposite** $\angle P$?
cues.working: $PQ$ is the **hypotenuse** and $QR$ is **opposite** $\angle P$, so use sine: $QR = 10\sin 50^\circ \approx 7.66$.

m10c-2-3-b.title: Solving Right Triangles, Part 2: From Two Sides, and in Context

cues.prompt: A right triangle has legs of $5$ and $12$. What is the angle ${\theta}$ **opposite** the side of length $5$?
cues.working: $5$ is **opposite** $\theta$ and $12$ is **adjacent**, so use tangent: $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\tfrac{5}{12}\right) \approx 22.6^\circ$. Neither leg is the hypotenuse, so sine and cosine do not fit.

cues.prompt: From the top of a $45$ m building, the angle of depression to a car is ${32^\circ}$. How far is the car from the base of the building?
cues.working: The angle of elevation from the car is also $32^\circ$ (alternate angles). The height $45$ m is **opposite** it and the distance $x$ is **adjacent**, so $\tan 32^\circ = \dfrac{45}{x}$ and $x = \dfrac{45}{\tan 32^\circ} \approx 72.0$ m.

chapters.title: Two boats on the same side

cues.prompt: From $40$ m away, the angles of elevation to the bottom and the top of a sign on a roof are ${28^\circ}$ and ${33^\circ}$. How tall is the sign?
cues.working: To the top: $40\tan 33^\circ \approx 25.98$ m. To the bottom: $40\tan 28^\circ \approx 21.27$ m. The triangles are stacked, so subtract: $25.98 - 21.27 \approx 4.7$ m. (Subtracting the angles first, $40\tan 5^\circ \approx 3.5$ m, is a common mistake.)

m10c-3-1.title: Prime Factors, GCF and LCM, Part 1: Prime Factorization

cues.prompt: What is the prime factorization of $84$?

m10c-3-1-b.title: Prime Factors, GCF and LCM, Part 2: GCF and LCM

cues.prompt: Hot dogs come in packs of $10$ and buns in packs of $8$. What is the smallest number of each you can buy to have the same number of hot dogs and buns?
cues.working: $10 = 2 \times 5$ and $8 = 2^3$, so $\text{LCM} = 2^3 \times 5 = 40$: four packs of hot dogs and five packs of buns.

m10c-3-2.title: Squares, Cubes and Their Roots, Part 1: Perfect Squares and Perfect Cubes

cues.prompt: Which of these is a perfect cube?
cues.working: Every exponent in $2^3 \times 5^3$ is divisible by 3: it is $(2 \times 5)^3 = 10^3 = 1000$.

m10c-3-2-b.title: Squares, Cubes and Their Roots, Part 2: Square Roots and Cube Roots

cues.prompt: A cube-shaped box has a volume of $3375\text{ cm}^3$. What is its edge length?

m10c-3-3.title: The Real Number System, Part 1: Rational and Irrational Numbers

cues.prompt: Which number is irrational?
cues.working: $12$ is not a perfect square, so $\sqrt{12} = 3.4641\ldots$ never terminates or repeats. The others are $\tfrac23$, $\tfrac13$ and $-2$.

m10c-3-3-b.title: The Real Number System, Part 2: Radicals, Estimating and Ordering

cues.prompt: Between which two whole numbers is $\sqrt{90}$?

m10c-3-4.title: Mixed and Entire Radicals, Part 1: Simplifying Radicals

cues.prompt: Write $\sqrt{48}$ in simplest form.
cues.working: The largest perfect square factor of $48$ is $16$: $\sqrt{48} = \sqrt{16 \times 3} = 4\sqrt{3}$.

m10c-3-4-b.title: Mixed and Entire Radicals, Part 2: Entire Radicals and Comparing

cues.prompt: Which is greater, $5\sqrt{2}$ or $4\sqrt{3}$?
choices: You cannot tell without a calculator.

m10c-3-5.title: Integral Exponents, Part 1: The Exponent Laws

cues.prompt: Simplify $(2x^4)^3$.

m10c-3-5-b.title: Integral Exponents, Part 2: Zero and Negative Exponents

cues.prompt: Evaluate $5^{-2}$.

m10c-3-6.title: Rational Exponents, Part 1: Exponents and Radicals

cues.prompt: Evaluate $32^{\frac35}$.

m10c-3-6-b.title: Rational Exponents, Part 2: The Exponent Laws with Rational Exponents

cues.prompt: Simplify $\left(27x^9\right)^{\frac13}$.
cues.working: $27^{\frac13} = \sqrt[3]{27} = 3$ and $x^{9 \times \frac13} = x^3$, so the answer is $3x^3$.

m10c-4-1.title: Multiplying Binomials, Part 1: Area Models and Algebra Tiles

cues.prompt: Expand $(x + 4)(x + 1)$.
cues.working: The tiles are one $x^2$, one $x$ and four more $x$ tiles, and four units: $x^2 + x + 4x + 4 = x^2 + 5x + 4$.

m10c-4-1-b.title: Multiplying Binomials, Part 2: The Distributive Property

m10c-4-2-b.title: Multiplying Polynomials, Part 2: Simplifying and Checking

cues.prompt: A student says $(x + 5)^2 = x^2 + 25$. Substitute $x = 2$. What do the two sides give?
cues.working: $(2 + 5)^2 = 49$ but $2^2 + 25 = 29$. The values differ, so it is wrong: $(x + 5)^2 = x^2 + 10x + 25$.

m10c-4-3.title: Common Factors, Part 1: Factoring Out the GCF

cues.prompt: Factor $10x^2 - 15x$ completely.

m10c-4-3-b.title: Common Factors, Part 2: Negative and Binomial Common Factors

cues.prompt: Factor $x(x - 7) - 2(x - 7)$.
cues.working: Both terms share $(x - 7)$. What is left is $x$ and $-2$: $(x - 7)(x - 2)$.

m10c-4-4.title: Factoring x² + bx + c, Part 1: The Product and Sum

cues.prompt: Factor $x^2 + 8x + 12$.

m10c-4-4-b.title: Factoring x² + bx + c, Part 2: Using the Signs

cues.prompt: Factor $x^2 - 3x - 28$.
cues.working: The product is $-28$ and the sum is $-3$: $-7$ and $4$.

choices: It is driving at a steady speed.
It is driving on flat ground.
cues.working: A horizontal segment means the distance from home is not changing, so the car is not moving.

m10c-5-1-b.title: Graphs That Tell a Story, Part 2: Sketching, and Continuous or Discrete

cues.prompt: Which data is discrete?
choices: The number of people in a room
cues.working: You cannot have $2.5$ people, so the count is discrete. Temperature, height and time can take any value in between.

cues.prompt: An arrow diagram has arrows $1 \to 5$, $2 \to 5$ and $3 \to 7$. Which set of ordered pairs shows the same relation?
cues.working: Each arrow becomes an ordered pair, from its start to its end.

m10c-5-2-b.title: Relations, Part 2: Independent and Dependent Variables

cues.prompt: The time it takes to fill a pool depends on how fast the water flows. Which is the independent variable?
cues.working: The time depends on the flow rate, so the flow rate is the independent variable.

m10c-5-3.title: Functions, Domain and Range, Part 1: What Is a Function?

cues.prompt: Which relation is a function?
cues.working: In A each input appears once; repeated outputs are fine. B and C repeat an input with different outputs.

m10c-5-3-b.title: Functions, Domain and Range, Part 2: Domain and Range

cues.prompt: A graph starts with a closed dot at $(1, 2)$ and goes up to the right forever. What is its domain?
cues.working: The closed dot includes $x = 1$, and the graph goes on forever to the right: $[1, \infty)$.

m10c-6-1.title: Linear Relations, Part 1: A Constant Rate of Change

cues.prompt: A taxi charges \$4 plus \$2 per kilometre. What is the rate of change of the cost?
cues.working: Each extra kilometre adds \$2: the rate of change is \$2 per km. The \$4 is the starting fee.

m10c-6-1-b.title: Linear Relations, Part 2: Tables, Equations and Rates

cues.prompt: Which equation is linear?
cues.working: In $3x - 4y = 12$ both variables are to the first power and are not multiplied together.

m10c-6-2-b.title: Characteristics of Linear Relations, Part 2: Domain, Range and Meaning

cues.prompt: A candle is $30\text{ cm}$ tall and burns $2\text{ cm}$ per hour: $h = 30 - 2t$. What does the $t$-intercept mean?
choices: The candle burns out after $15$ hours.
The candle burns $2\text{ cm}$ each hour.
The candle burns out after $30$ hours.
cues.working: At the $t$-intercept, $h = 0$: $0 = 30 - 2t$, so $t = 15$. The candle has burned down after $15$ hours.

m10c-6-4.title: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines, Part 1: Their Slopes

cues.prompt: A line has slope $-\tfrac27$. What is the slope of a line perpendicular to it?
cues.working: Flip $-\dfrac27$ and change the sign: $\dfrac72$. Check: $-\dfrac27 \times \dfrac72 = -1$.

m10c-6-4-b.title: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines, Part 2: Classifying and Finding Unknowns

cues.prompt: Line 1 has slope $3$. Line 2 passes through $(2, k)$ and $(4, 1)$. Find $k$ so the lines are parallel.
cues.working: Parallel lines have equal slopes: $\dfrac{1 - k}{4 - 2} = 3$, so $1 - k = 6$ and $k = -5$.

cues.prompt: A line crosses the $y$-axis at $-2$ and passes through $(4, 1)$. What is its equation?
cues.working: $b = -2$. From $(0, -2)$ to $(4, 1)$: rise $3$, run $4$, so $m = \tfrac34$ and $y = \tfrac34 x - 2$.

m10c-7-3.title: General Form, Part 1: Converting to General Form

cues.prompt: Write $y = \tfrac34 x + 2$ in general form.
cues.working: Multiply by $4$: $4y = 3x + 8$. Move every term left: $-3x + 4y - 8 = 0$. Make $A$ positive: $3x - 4y + 8 = 0$.

m10c-7-3-b.title: General Form, Part 2: Slopes, Intercepts and Equivalent Forms

cues.prompt: What is the slope of $2x - 6y + 3 = 0$?

m10c-7-4.title: Writing Equations, Part 1: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines

A gym charges a joining fee plus a monthly fee. Three months cost \$140 and seven months cost \$260. What is the joining fee?
cues.working: Rate: $\dfrac{260 - 140}{7 - 3} = 30$ dollars per month. Then $140 = 30(3) + b$, so $b = 50$.

m10c-7-5.title: Lines of Best Fit, Part 1: Scatterplots and Trends

cues.prompt: As the outside temperature rises, sales of hot chocolate tend to fall. What kind of correlation is this?
cues.working: As one variable increases, the other tends to decrease: a negative correlation.

m10c-7-5-b.title: Lines of Best Fit, Part 2: Equations and Predictions

cues.prompt: A line of best fit for data from $x = 1$ to $x = 10$ is $y = 2x + 3$. Predict $y$ when $x = 6$.
cues.working: $y = 2(6) + 3 = 15$. Since $6$ is between $1$ and $10$, this is interpolation.

m10c-8-1.title: Systems of Linear Equations, Part 1: Modelling and Verifying

cues.prompt: Is $(3, -1)$ the solution of the system $x + y = 2$ and $2x - y = 5$?
choices: No: it does not satisfy $2x - y = 5$.
No: it does not satisfy $x + y = 2$.
cues.working: $3 + (-1) = 2$ is true, but $2(3) - (-1) = 7$, not $5$. So $(3, -1)$ is not the solution.

m10c-8-1-b.title: Systems of Linear Equations, Part 2: Solving by Graphing

cues.prompt: Which point is the solution of $y = 2x - 1$ and $y = -x + 5$?

cues.prompt: Solve the system $y = x + 2$ and $2x + y = 11$.

m10c-8-2-b.title: Solving by Substitution, Part 2: Isolating First and Fractions

cues.prompt: Solve the system $x - y = 3$ and $2x + 4y = 3$.

m10c-8-3.title: Solving by Elimination, Part 1: Adding Equations

cues.prompt: Solve the system $x + 2y = 7$ and $3x - 2y = 5$.

m10c-8-3-b.title: Solving by Elimination, Part 2: Multiplying Both and Choosing a Method

cues.prompt: Solve the system $2x + 5y = 1$ and $3x + 2y = -4$.
cues.working: Multiply by $3$ and $2$: $6x + 15y = 3$ and $6x + 4y = -8$. Subtract: $11y = 11$, so $y = 1$. Then $2x + 5 = 1$, so $x = -2$.

m10c-8-4.title: The Number of Solutions, Part 1: One, None or Infinitely Many

cues.prompt: How many solutions does the system $3x + y = 4$ and $6x + 2y = 8$ have?
cues.working: The second equation is the first multiplied by $2$, so both describe the same line.

m103-1-1.title: Rates and Proportions, Part 1: Ratios, Rates and Unit Rates

cues.prompt: A courier drives $207\text{ km}$ in $2$ h $15$ min. What is the average speed?
cues.working: $15\text{ min} = 0.25\text{ h}$, so the time is $2.25\text{ h}$, and $207 \div 2.25 = 92\text{ km/h}$.

m103-1-1-b.title: Rates and Proportions, Part 2: Proportions on the Job

cues.prompt: A pickup uses $11.2\text{ L}$ per $100\text{ km}$, and gas costs \$1.52 per litre. What does gas cost for a $420\text{ km}$ trip?

m103-1-2.title: Unit Price and Best Buys, Part 1: Finding a Unit Price

cues.prompt: A $1.5\text{ L}$ bottle of dish soap costs \$6.30. What is the unit price per $100\text{ mL}$?
cues.working: $1.5\text{ L} = 1500\text{ mL}$, which is $15$ groups of $100\text{ mL}$. Then $6.30 \div 15 = 0.42$ dollars.

m103-1-2-b.title: Unit Price and Best Buys, Part 2: The Best Buy

cues.prompt: Coffee costs \$7.49 for $340\text{ g}$ or \$19.99 for $925\text{ g}$. Which is the better buy?
choices: The $925\text{ g}$ bag, at about \$2.16 per $100\text{ g}$
The $340\text{ g}$ bag, at about \$2.20 per $100\text{ g}$
The $340\text{ g}$ bag, because it costs less
They cost the same per gram
cues.working: $7.49 \div 3.4 \approx 2.20$ and $19.99 \div 9.25 \approx 2.16$ dollars per $100\text{ g}$, so the big bag is slightly cheaper per unit.

m103-1-3.title: Markups, Sales and Taxes, Part 1: Percent Change, Markups and Discounts

cues.prompt: A drill is regularly \$120 and is on sale for $15\%$ off. What is the sale price?

m103-1-3-b.title: Markups, Sales and Taxes, Part 2: Two Discounts and Sales Tax

cues.working: The rate starts with US dollars, but you have CAD, so divide: $270 \div 1.35 = 200$.

m103-1-4-b.title: Currency Exchange, Part 2: Buy Rates, Sell Rates and Fees

cues.prompt: Using the table (bank buys euros at $1.4870$ CAD, sells at $1.5810$ CAD), what does it cost to buy €250?
cues.working: You are buying euros, so the bank is selling: $250 \times 1.5810 = 395.25$ dollars.

m103-2-1.title: Hourly Wages and Overtime, Part 1: Gross Pay and Timecards

cues.prompt: A shift runs from 9:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with a 30-minute unpaid break, at \$16.80 per hour. What is the gross pay?
cues.working: 9:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 7 h 30 min. Minus 30 min: 7 h. Then $7 \times 16.80 = 117.60$ dollars.

m103-2-1-b.title: Hourly Wages and Overtime, Part 2: Overtime

cues.prompt: Lee earns \$20.00 per hour, with time-and-a-half for hours over 40 in a week. Lee worked 44 hours. What is the gross pay?
cues.working: $40 \times 20 = 800$, and $4 \times 30 = 120$, so the gross pay is $920$ dollars.

m103-2-2.title: Salary, Commission and Piecework, Part 1: Salary and Commission

cues.prompt: A salary of \$46,800 a year is paid weekly. How much is each pay cheque?

m103-2-2-b.title: Salary, Commission and Piecework, Part 2: Graduated Commission and Piecework

cues.prompt: A salesperson earns 2% on the first \$20,000 of sales and 6% on sales above \$20,000. Sales were \$35,000. What is the commission?
cues.working: $0.02 \times 20{,}000 = 400$, and $0.06 \times 15{,}000 = 900$, so the commission is $1300$ dollars.

m103-2-3.title: Comparing Pay and Contracts, Part 1: Job Offers and Break-Even

cues.prompt: Job A pays \$900 a week. Job B pays \$300 a week plus 8% of sales. What weekly sales make them pay the same?

m103-2-3-b.title: Comparing Pay and Contracts, Part 2: Working on Contract

m103-2-4.title: Deductions and Net Pay, Part 1: From Gross to Net

cues.prompt: Gross pay is \$800. Income tax is 15% of gross pay above \$500. What is the income tax?

m103-2-4-b.title: Deductions and Net Pay, Part 2: Take-Home Pay and Working Backward

cues.prompt: A job pays \$1,500 a month plus 5% commission. What monthly sales give earnings of \$2,700?

m103-3-1.title: SI Units, Part 1: Prefixes and Converting

cues.prompt: A truck carries $4.2$ tonnes of gravel. How many kilograms is that?
cues.working: $1\text{ t} = 1000\text{ kg}$. Kilograms are smaller, so multiply: $4.2 \times 1000 = 4200\text{ kg}$.

m103-3-1-b.title: SI Units, Part 2: Mixed Units, Volume and Capacity

cues.prompt: A cattle trough is $2.4\text{ m}$ long, $60\text{ cm}$ wide and $50\text{ cm}$ deep. How many litres does it hold?
A pipe is $103\text{ in}$ long. What is this in feet and inches?
cues.working: $103 \div 12 = 8$ remainder $7$, since $8 \times 12 = 96$. So $103\text{ in} = 8\text{ ft } 7\text{ in}$.

m103-3-2-b.title: Imperial Units, Part 2: Mass and Capacity

cues.prompt: A recipe needs $5$ US quarts of stock. How many cups is that?
cues.working: $1\text{ qt} = 2\text{ pt} = 4$ cups, so $5\text{ qt} = 5 \times 4 = 20$ cups.

m103-3-3.title: Converting Between Systems, Part 1: Conversion Factors

cues.prompt: A trip is $240\text{ km}$. About how many miles is it? Use $1\text{ mi} \approx 1.609\text{ km}$.
cues.working: Miles are bigger than kilometres, so divide: $240 \div 1.609 \approx 149\text{ mi}$.

m103-3-3-b.title: Converting Between Systems, Part 2: Imperial to SI and Estimates

cues.prompt: A board is $8\text{ ft}$ long. How long is it in centimetres? Use $1\text{ ft} = 30.48\text{ cm}$.
cues.working: Centimetres are smaller, so multiply: $8 \times 30.48 = 243.84\text{ cm}$.

cues.prompt: A hot tub is set to $40^\circ\text{C}$. What is that in degrees Fahrenheit?

m103-3-4-b.title: Temperature, Part 2: Fahrenheit to Celsius, Estimates and Changes

cues.prompt: A coolant gauge reads $230^\circ\text{F}$. What is that in degrees Celsius?

m103-4-1.title: Rulers and Tape Measures, Part 1: Precision and Metric Rulers

cues.prompt: A washer lies along a ruler from the $3.7\text{ cm}$ mark to the $5.2\text{ cm}$ mark. How wide is it, in millimetres?

m103-4-1-b.title: Rulers and Tape Measures, Part 2: Imperial Rulers

cues.prompt: A bar ends $10$ sixteenths past the $2$ in mark. How long is it?
cues.working: $\tfrac{10}{16} = \tfrac58$, so the bar is $2\tfrac58$ in long.

m103-4-2.title: Working with Fractional Measurements, Part 1: Adding and Subtracting Inches

cues.prompt: Find $5\tfrac38 - 1\tfrac{11}{16}$ in.

m103-4-2-b.title: Working with Fractional Measurements, Part 2: Saw Kerf, Feet and Inches

cues.prompt: A wall is $11\text{ ft } 3\text{ in}$ long. A cabinet run takes $6\text{ ft } 8\text{ in}$. How much wall is left?
cues.working: $11\text{ ft } 3\text{ in} = 10\text{ ft } 15\text{ in}$, and $10\text{ ft } 15\text{ in} - 6\text{ ft } 8\text{ in} = 4\text{ ft } 7\text{ in}$.

cues.prompt: A rectangular window is $1.2\text{ m}$ wide and $90\text{ cm}$ tall. How much trim goes around it?

m103-4-3-b.title: Perimeter and Circumference, Part 2: Circumference and Working Backward

cues.prompt: A round table has a radius of $0.6\text{ m}$. How much edging goes around it, to the nearest hundredth of a metre?

m103-4-4.title: Cutting and Buying Material, Part 1: How Many Pieces?

cues.prompt: How many $60\text{ cm}$ pieces can be cut from a $4\text{ m}$ rod, ignoring the kerf?
cues.working: $400 \div 60 \approx 6.67$. Round down: $6$ whole pieces, with $40\text{ cm}$ left over.

m103-4-4-b.title: Cutting and Buying Material, Part 2: Buying by Length

cues.prompt: Fencing costs \$8.75 per linear metre. A rectangular yard is $20\text{ m}$ by $15\text{ m}$, with a $1\text{ m}$ gate that needs no fencing. What does the fencing cost, before tax?
cues.working: $P = 2(20 + 15) = 70\text{ m}$, minus the gate: $69\text{ m}$. Then $69 \times 8.75 = 603.75$ dollars.

m103-5-1.title: Area of Common Shapes, Part 1: Rectangles, Triangles and Trapezoids

cues.prompt: A triangular sail has a base of $12\text{ m}$ and a perpendicular height of $5\text{ m}$. Its slanted side is $7\text{ m}$. What is its area?

m103-5-1-b.title: Area of Common Shapes, Part 2: Circles and Working Backward

cues.prompt: A circular patio has an area of $50\text{ m}^2$. What is its radius, to the nearest tenth of a metre?

m103-5-2.title: Composite and Irregular Areas, Part 1: Composite Shapes

cues.prompt: A garage wall is $20\text{ ft}$ by $9\text{ ft}$, with a door $16\text{ ft}$ by $7\text{ ft}$. What area of wall is left to paint?

m103-5-2-b.title: Composite and Irregular Areas, Part 2: Irregular Shapes

cues.prompt: On a grid of $1\text{ m}^2$ squares, a pond covers $20$ full squares and $12$ partly covered squares. Estimate its area.
cues.working: Full squares plus half of the partly covered ones: $20 + 12 \div 2 = 26\text{ m}^2$.

m103-5-3.title: Surface Area, Part 1: Boxes and the Faces You Need

cues.prompt: A closed box is $10\text{ cm}$ by $8\text{ cm}$ by $5\text{ cm}$. What is its surface area?
A closed can has a radius of $4\text{ cm}$ and a height of $10\text{ cm}$. What is its surface area, to the nearest square centimetre?

m103-5-4.title: Area Units and Material Costs, Part 1: Square Units

cues.prompt: A patio is $36\text{ ft}^2$. How many square yards is that?
cues.working: $1\text{ yd}^2 = 9\text{ ft}^2$, and square yards are bigger, so divide: $36 \div 9 = 4\text{ yd}^2$.

m103-5-4-b.title: Area Units and Material Costs, Part 2: How Much to Buy

cues.prompt: A floor is $200\text{ ft}^2$. Add 10% for waste. Each box of tile covers $15\text{ ft}^2$. How many boxes are needed?
What kind of angle measures $181^\circ$?
cues.working: $181^\circ$ is more than $180^\circ$, so it is reflex. Only exactly $180^\circ$ is a straight angle.

cues.prompt: Three angles meet at a point. Two of them measure $150^\circ$ and $95^\circ$. What does the third angle measure?
cues.working: Angles around a point add to $360^\circ$: $360^\circ - (150^\circ + 95^\circ) = 360^\circ - 245^\circ = 115^\circ$.

m103-6-2.title: Angle Relationships, Part 1: Complementary and Supplementary

cues.prompt: An angle measures $38^\circ$. What is its complement?

m103-6-2-b.title: Angle Relationships, Part 2: Vertically Opposite Angles and Bisectors

cues.prompt: Two vertically opposite angles measure $(4x + 5)^\circ$ and $(2x + 45)^\circ$. What is $x$?
cues.working: They are equal: $4x + 5 = 2x + 45$, so $2x = 40$ and $x = 20$. Each angle is $85^\circ$.

m103-6-3.title: Parallel Lines, Part 1: Transversals and Angle Pairs

cues.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. Which pair of angles **add to** $180^\circ$?
cues.working: Co-interior angles (same side, between the lines) add to $180^\circ$. The other pairs are equal.

m103-6-3-b.title: Parallel Lines, Part 2: Finding Angles and Testing for Parallel

cues.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. A pair of alternate interior angles measure $(2x + 30)^\circ$ and $(4x - 10)^\circ$. What is $x$?
cues.working: Alternate interior angles are equal: $2x + 30 = 4x - 10$, so $40 = 2x$ and $x = 20$. Each angle is $70^\circ$.

m103-6-4.title: Spatial Puzzles, Part 1: Counting Squares and Rectangles

cues.prompt: How many squares, of all sizes, are in a $4 \times 4$ grid?
cues.working: $16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 30$ squares: sixteen $1 \times 1$, nine $2 \times 2$, four $3 \times 3$ and one $4 \times 4$.

m103-6-4-b.title: Spatial Puzzles, Part 2: Painted Cubes and Dice

cues.prompt: A $3\text{ cm}$ cube is painted on all six faces, then cut into $1\text{ cm}$ cubes. How many small cubes have exactly **two** painted faces?
cues.working: Each of the $12$ edges has $3 - 2 = 1$ middle cube: $12 \times 1 = 12$.

m103-7-1.title: The Pythagorean Theorem, Part 1: Finding the Hypotenuse

cues.prompt: A right triangle has legs of $9\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$. How long is the hypotenuse?

m103-7-1-b.title: The Pythagorean Theorem, Part 2: Finding a Leg and Checking for Square

cues.prompt: The hypotenuse of a right triangle is $10\text{ m}$ and one leg is $6\text{ m}$. How long is the other leg?

m103-7-2.title: Pythagorean Problems, Part 1: Ladders and Rafters

cues.prompt: A $13\text{ ft}$ ladder leans against a wall with its foot $5\text{ ft}$ from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
cues.working: The ladder is the hypotenuse: $h^2 = 13^2 - 5^2 = 169 - 25 = 144$, so $h = 12\text{ ft}$.

m103-7-2-b.title: Pythagorean Problems, Part 2: Diagonals and Two-Step Problems

cues.prompt: A TV screen is $32\text{ in}$ wide and $18\text{ in}$ tall. What size is it, to the nearest inch?

m103-7-3.title: Similar Polygons, Part 1: Same Shape, Different Size

cues.prompt: Rectangle P is $10\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$. Which rectangle is similar to P?
cues.working: $\tfrac{15}{10} = 1.5$ and $\tfrac{6}{4} = 1.5$: the ratios are equal. For B, $\tfrac{12}{10} = 1.2$ but $\tfrac{6}{4} = 1.5$.

m103-7-3-b.title: Similar Polygons, Part 2: The Scale Factor

m103-8-1.title: The Tangent Ratio, Part 1: Naming the Sides

cues.prompt: In a right triangle, the side opposite $\theta$ is $9$, the side adjacent to $\theta$ is $12$ and the hypotenuse is $15$. What is $\tan\theta$?

m103-8-1-b.title: The Tangent Ratio, Part 2: Finding Sides and Angles

cues.prompt: A ramp rises $0.8\text{ m}$ over a horizontal run of $6\text{ m}$. What angle does it make with the ground, to the nearest tenth of a degree?

m103-8-2.title: Sine and Cosine, Part 1: Choosing the Ratio

cues.prompt: A $4\text{ m}$ ladder makes a $70^\circ$ angle with the ground. You want the distance from the wall to its foot. Which ratio should you use?
cues.working: The ladder is the hypotenuse, and the distance along the ground touches the $70^\circ$ angle, so it is adjacent. Adjacent and hypotenuse: CAH, cosine.

m103-8-2-b.title: Sine and Cosine, Part 2: Finding Sides and Angles

cues.prompt: A $4\text{ m}$ ladder makes a $70^\circ$ angle with the ground. How far is its foot from the wall, to the nearest tenth of a metre?
cues.working: The distance is adjacent and the ladder is the hypotenuse: $d = 4\cos 70^\circ \approx 1.4\text{ m}$.

m103-8-3.title: Trigonometry on the Job, Part 1: Elevation and Depression

cues.prompt: From the top of a $20\text{ m}$ cliff, a boat is at an angle of depression of $30^\circ$. How far is the boat from the base of the cliff?
cues.working: The angle at the boat is also $30^\circ$. The height is opposite and the distance is adjacent: $d = \dfrac{20}{\tan 30^\circ} \approx 34.6\text{ m}$.

m103-8-3-b.title: Trigonometry on the Job, Part 2: Roofs, Ramps and Ladders

cues.prompt: A $10\text{ m}$ ladder is set at $75^\circ$ to the ground. How high up the wall does it reach, to the nearest tenth of a metre?
cues.working: The height is opposite and the ladder is the hypotenuse: $h = 10 \sin 75^\circ \approx 9.7\text{ m}$.

m104-1-1.title: Place Value, Part 1: Reading and Writing Numbers

cues.prompt: What is the value of the $8$ in $38{,}516$?
cues.working: The $8$ is in the thousands place, so it is worth $8 \times 1{,}000 = 8{,}000$.

m104-1-1-b.title: Place Value, Part 2: Comparing and Rounding

cues.prompt: Round $7{,}952$ to the nearest hundred.
cues.working: The hundreds digit is $9$ and the digit to its right is $5$, so round up. One more hundred than $7{,}900$ is $8{,}000$.

m104-1-2.title: The Four Operations, Part 1: Choosing the Operation

cues.prompt: Each shelf holds $15$ boxes. How many shelves do you need for $100$ boxes?
cues.working: $100 \div 15 = 6$ remainder $10$. The $10$ extra boxes still need a shelf, so round up to $7$.

m104-1-2-b.title: The Four Operations, Part 2: The Order of Operations

cues.prompt: Find the value of $18 - 4 \times 3$.

m104-2-1.title: Fractions, Part 1: Parts of a Whole

cues.prompt: Fill in the missing number: $\dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{?}{12}$
cues.working: The bottom changed from $3$ to $12$, which is $\times 4$. Do the same to the top: $2 \times 4 = 8$.

m104-2-1-b.title: Fractions, Part 2: Lowest Terms and Comparing

cues.prompt: Which is bigger: $\dfrac{3}{4}$ inch or $\dfrac{11}{16}$ inch?
A crew of $30$ workers is told that $\dfrac{2}{5}$ of them work the night shift. How many work nights?

m104-2-3-b.title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions, Part 2: Mixed Numbers

m104-3-1.title: Decimals and Money, Part 1: Place Value, Adding and Subtracting

cues.working: Write $5.6$ as $5.60$, line up the points, and subtract: $5.60 - 2.35 = 3.25$.

m104-3-1-b.title: Decimals and Money, Part 2: Multiplying, Dividing and Making Change

Write $\dfrac{2}{5}$ as a percent.

m104-3-3.title: Percents of Money, Part 1: Percent of an Amount and Tips

cues.prompt: A haircut costs \$32. You leave a $20\%$ tip. How much is the tip?

m104-3-3-b.title: Percents of Money, Part 2: Discounts and GST

cues.prompt: A shirt costs \$40 and is $25\%$ off. Then $5\%$ GST is added. What is the total?
cues.working: Discount: $0.25 \times 40 = 10$, so the sale price is \$30. GST: $0.05 \times 30 = 1.50$. Total: \$31.50.

cues.prompt: Which temperature is the coldest?
cues.working: $-12$ is farthest left on a number line, so it is the least, and the coldest.

m104-5-1.title: Patterns, Part 1: Tables and Extending Patterns

cues.prompt: What is the next term? $3, \; 6, \; 12, \; 24, \; \ldots$
cues.working: The jumps are $3, 6, 12$, so it is not adding. Each term doubles: $24 \times 2 = 48$.

cues.prompt: A pattern goes $7, \; 11, \; 15, \; 19, \; \ldots$ for $n = 1, 2, 3, 4$. Which rule fits?
cues.working: The jump is $4$, so the rule starts with $4n$. When $n = 1$, $4n = 4$, and $7 - 4 = 3$. So $y = 4n + 3$.

m104-5-2.title: Expressions and Formulas, Part 1: Variables and Expressions

cues.prompt: A gym charges a \$25 sign-up fee plus \$30 per month. Which expression gives the cost for $m$ months?
cues.working: The monthly part changes with $m$: $30m$. The sign-up fee is paid once: $+\,25$.

m104-5-2-b.title: Expressions and Formulas, Part 2: Using Formulas

cues.prompt: Use $C = 5 + 3k$ to find the cost $C$ when $k = 8$.
Solve $5x + 3 = 38$.
On Jordan’s pay graph, the line goes from \$0 at 0 hours to \$160 at 8 hours. How much does Jordan earn for 3 hours?
cues.working: The pay goes up \$20 each hour: $3 \times 20 = 60$.

m104-6-1.title: Metric Units, Part 1: Choosing and Estimating

cues.prompt: Which is the best estimate for the height of a classroom door?
cues.working: A door is a little taller than an adult, about two big steps: $2\text{ m}$.

cues.prompt: A bag of flour has a mass of $2.5\text{ kg}$. How many grams is that?
cues.working: Kilograms to grams is big to small, so multiply: $2.5 \times 1000 = 2500\text{ g}$.

cues.prompt: On a ruler with $16$ spaces in each inch, a screw ends $6$ spaces past the $1$-inch mark. How long is it?
cues.working: $1\tfrac{6}{16}$ in, and $\tfrac{6}{16} = \tfrac{3}{8}$, so the screw is $1\tfrac{3}{8}$ in long.

m104-6-3.title: Time and Temperature, Part 1: Elapsed Time

cues.prompt: A shift runs from 9:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. How long is it?
cues.working: 9:30 to 10:00 is 30 min, 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 7 h. Total: 7 h 30 min.

m104-6-3-b.title: Time and Temperature, Part 2: Reading Temperatures

cues.prompt: It was $3^\circ\text{C}$ at noon and $-8^\circ\text{C}$ at midnight. How many degrees did the temperature drop?
cues.working: From $3$ down to $0$ is $3$ degrees, and from $0$ down to $-8$ is $8$ more: $3 + 8 = 11$.

cues.prompt: A square patio has sides of $3.5\text{ m}$. What is its perimeter?
cues.working: A square has four equal sides: $P = 4 \times 3.5 = 14\text{ m}$.

m104-8-1.title: Angles and Shapes, Part 1: Types of Angles

cues.prompt: Two angles make a straight line. One is $125^\circ$. What is the other?
cues.working: Angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$: $180 - 125 = 55^\circ$.

m104-8-1-b.title: Angles and Shapes, Part 2: Triangles and Quadrilaterals

cues.prompt: A triangle has sides of $5\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$ and $9\text{ cm}$. Name it by its sides.
cues.working: No two sides are equal, so the triangle is scalene.

m104-8-2.title: 3-D Objects, Part 1: Faces, Edges and Vertices

cues.prompt: A square pyramid has a square base and $4$ triangle faces. How many edges does it have?
cues.working: $4$ edges around the base and $4$ going up to the top: $4 + 4 = 8$ edges.

cues.prompt: In a top view, one column has a stack of $4$ boxes with a stack of $1$ box behind it. How many boxes high is that column in the front view?
cues.working: The front view shows the tallest stack in the column: $4$ boxes.

m104-8-3.title: Symmetry and Transformations, Part 1: Lines of Symmetry

cues.prompt: A triangular road sign has $3$ equal sides and nothing written on it. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
cues.working: A fold from each corner to the middle of the opposite side makes the halves match: $3$ lines.

m104-8-3-b.title: Symmetry and Transformations, Part 2: Slides, Flips and Turns

cues.prompt: A game piece at $(3, 1)$ slides $2$ units left and $4$ units up. Where is its image?
cues.working: Left subtracts from $x$: $3 - 2 = 1$. Up adds to $y$: $1 + 4 = 5$. The image is $(1, 5)$.

m104-9-1.title: Data and Graphs, Part 1: Tallies and Bar Graphs

cues.prompt: The grid lines on a bar graph go up by $4$. A bar stops halfway between the lines for $12$ and $16$. What value does it show?

cues.prompt: A school asks whether to build a new sports field. Which sample is fair?
choices: $30$ students picked at random from the school list
cues.working: Picking at random from the whole school gives every student the same chance to be asked.

cues.prompt: Find the median of $9$, $4$, $7$, $12$ and $5$.
cues.working: In order: $4,\ 5,\ 7,\ 9,\ 12$. The middle value is $7$.

m104-9-2-b.title: Averages, Part 2: Mode, Range and Outliers

cues.prompt: Find the range of $14$, $9$, $21$, $9$ and $17$.

m104-9-3.title: Probability, Part 1: How Likely Is It?

cues.prompt: A box has $4$ cherry, $7$ lemon and $9$ lime candies. What is the probability of picking lemon?

m104-9-3-b.title: Probability, Part 2: Percents and Comparing Chances

cues.prompt: Bag C has $8$ marbles and $2$ are red. Bag D has $12$ marbles and $4$ are red. Which bag gives the better chance of red?
cues.working: Bag C: $\dfrac{2}{8} = 25\%$. Bag D: $\dfrac{4}{12} \approx 33.3\%$. Bag D is better.

m201-2-3.title: The Sine Law, Part 1: Finding Sides

cues.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A = 40^\circ$, $\angle C = 75^\circ$ and $a = 8$ cm. Which equation gives $c$?

m201-2-3-b.title: The Sine Law, Part 2: Finding Angles

cues.prompt: $\sin B = 0.5$ and $\angle B$ is obtuse. What is $\angle B$?
cues.working: $\sin^{-1}(0.5) = 30^\circ$, and the obtuse angle with the same sine is $180^\circ - 30^\circ = 150^\circ$.

m201-2-4.title: The Ambiguous Case, Part 1: How Many Triangles?

cues.prompt: $\angle A = 40^\circ$, $b = 10$ cm and $a = 8$ cm. How many triangles are possible?
cues.working: $h = 10\sin 40^\circ \approx 6.43$, and $6.43 < 8 < 10$, so there are two triangles.

m201-2-5-b.title: The Cosine Law, Part 2: Finding Angles and Choosing a Law

cues.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$, $a = 8$, $b = 5$ and $c = 6$. Which expression gives $\cos A$?
cues.working: The side opposite $\angle A$, $a = 8$, is the one subtracted: $\cos A = \dfrac{25 + 36 - 64}{60} = -0.05$, so $\angle A \approx 92.9^\circ$.

m201-2-5-c.title: The Cosine Law, Part 3: Two-Step Problems

cues.prompt: A triangle has two sides of $10$ m and $14$ m, with a $35^\circ$ angle between them. Which law finds the third side?
cues.working: Two sides and the contained angle (SAS): there is no complete side–angle pair, so use the cosine law.

m201-3-1.title: Quadratic Functions in Vertex Form, Part 1: Transforming y = x²

cues.prompt: How is the graph of $y = (x + 5)^2 - 2$ related to the graph of $y = x^2$?
cues.working: $x + 5 = x - (-5)$, so $p = -5$: $5$ units left. $q = -2$: $2$ units down.

m201-3-1-b.title: Quadratic Functions in Vertex Form, Part 2: Reading the Features

cues.prompt: What is the vertex of $y = 3(x - 2)^2 + 7$, and is it a maximum or a minimum?
cues.working: $p = 2$ and $q = 7$, so the vertex is $(2, 7)$. $a = 3 > 0$, so the parabola opens up and $7$ is the minimum value.

m201-3-1-c.title: Quadratic Functions in Vertex Form, Part 3: Domain, Range and Models

cues.prompt: What is the range of $y = -(x - 1)^2 + 4$?
cues.working: The vertex is $(1, 4)$ and $a = -1 < 0$, so the parabola opens down and $4$ is the maximum value: $y \le 4$.

m201-3-4.title: Solving Optimization Problems, Part 1: Maximum and Minimum Values

cues.prompt: Two numbers have a sum of $20$. What is the largest possible product?
cues.working: The product $P = x(20 - x)$ has zeros $0$ and $20$, so the vertex is at $x = 10$. Both numbers are $10$, and $P = 100$.

m201-3-4-b.title: Solving Optimization Problems, Part 2: Area and Revenue

cues.prompt: In this example, a store sells $200$ shirts a week at \$10 each. For every \$1 increase in price, $10$ fewer shirts are sold. What price maximizes revenue?
cues.working: The zeros of $R(x) = (10 + x)(200 - 10x)$ are $x = -10$ and $x = 20$, so $x = 5$ and the price is \$15.
